conventions.convention: Flat spacetime uses signature (−,+,+,+), SI units and x⁰=ct. Observer energy is E_n(P)=−cη(P,n), and spatial momentum is q_n(P)=P+η(P,n)n.

Collision lists are finite and nonempty; every leg is nonzero future causal. Massive legs have recorded positive invariant mass; null legs have recorded mass zero and an independently specified momentum scale.
Isolated balance applies to complete incoming and outgoing lists at one event, with no external four-momentum transfer or omitted leg. It asserts no reaction occurrence or rate.
The work identity uses constant positive mass and one fixed inertial chart. The separate C¹ variable-mass ansatz supplies only η(P,K)=−m(dm/dτ)c² and adopts no mass evolution law.

For a timelike total with rest energy W, the two-body threshold is W≥(a+b)c² when both masses are positive, and W>(a+b)c² when either mass is zero. A zero four-vector is never an admissible null product.

load_bearing.statement: A finite nonempty sum of nonzero future-causal vectors is nonzero future causal, and is timelike if any summand is timelike. An all-null sum is null exactly when all summands lie on one future null ray. For timelike total Q, a center-of-momentum frame exists and M(Q)≥Σm_i, with equality exactly for an entirely massive list sharing one future unit timelike direction. A nonzero future-null total has no center-of-momentum frame.

For the stated C² future-timelike worldline, constant m>0 and fixed inertial chart, E=γmc²>0, p=γmv, E²=m²c⁴+c²|p|², v=c²p/E, dE/dt=F·v and K=γ(F·v/c,F). Separately, the stated C¹ variable-mass ansatz satisfies η(P,K)=−m(dm/dτ)c².
When the event is isolated and the incoming and outgoing lists contain every leg, Q_in=Q_out. This is a scoped reuse of clause (iii) of post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics.

For the complete isolated configuration satisfying balance, its common total Q is nonzero future causal. If Q is timelike, its invariant mass satisfies M≥μ_in and M≥μ_out; a null leg makes the corresponding inequality strict. Equality requires entirely massive co-moving legs. A null total permits only co-directed null legs and no positive-mass final leg.

For future-timelike total Q and W=Mc², a nonzero two-product state of masses a,b≥0 exists exactly at W≥(a+b)c² for a,b>0, and W>(a+b)c² otherwise. Its energies are E_a=[W²+(a²−b²)c⁴]/(2W), E_b=[W²+(b²−a²)c⁴]/(2W), and k²=[W²−(a+b)²c⁴][W²−(a−b)²c⁴]/(4W²c²).

published_dependencies.used_for: Constant-positive-mass momentum P=mU and the exact finite, complete isolated-collision balance reused by the local postulate.
Four-velocity normalization, observer rest-space geometry, relative velocity and the inertial-coordinate expression U=γ(c,v).
Future positively oriented orthonormal inertial bases and their affine coordinate charts.
The Euclidean spatial dot product and norm in the named laboratory frame.
Observer decomposition, invariant mass of a nonzero future-causal vector and constant-mass kinetic energy.
Finite total momentum, timelike invariant mass, the null-total mass convention and the definition of a center-of-momentum frame.
Finite nonempty collision lists, mass-specified on-shell legs and conservation as equality of side totals.
Positive observer energy, massive mass shells and E=c|q| for nonzero future-null momentum.
Future-cone coordinates, closure under finite sums and strict timelikeness when a summand is timelike.
Existence and unique time vector of a timelike total's rest frame, and absence of a rest frame for a nonzero null total.
Pairwise spatial inequalities and equality conditions in the classification of all-null finite sums.

seams_checked.note: Checked the earlier spacetime/worldline and mechanical-momentum definitions against their uses. The collision page preserves signature, SI normalization, pointwise observer projection, positive massive mass and independently scaled nonzero null momentum. Flat inertial work is kept separate from curved-background claims.

The prescribed-field trajectory theorem cites the inverse-momentum result in its Statement, L2 and proof step 1.1. Its V_c(p)=p/[m√(1+|p|²/(m²c²))] follows from the cited positive-energy mass shell and v=c²p/E. It retains constant m>0, C² future-timelike motion, a fixed inertial chart and explicit conditional reliance on the draft supplier.
